requirements.text: According to Article I Section 7, when can a bill become law without the President signing it,

claims.statement: According to Article I, Section 7, a bill can become a law without the President's signature if, after the President returns it with objections, two-thirds of both the originating House and the other House approve and pass it upon reconsideration.

evidence.quote: If after such Reconsideration two thirds of that House shall agree to pass the Bill, it shall be sent, together with the Objections, to the other House, by which it shall likewise be reconsidered, and if approved by two thirds of that House, it shall become a Law.

claims.statement: Additionally, a bill becomes a law in like manner as if the President had signed it if it is not returned by the President within ten days (Sundays excepted) after being presented.

evidence.quote: If any Bill shall not be returned by the President within ten Days (Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to him, the Same shall be a Law, in like Manner as if he had signed it,

requirements.text: and what exception can prevent that outcome?

claims.statement: The exception that prevents an unreturned bill from becoming a law is if Congress, by their adjournment, prevents its return.

evidence.quote: unless the Congress by their Adjournment prevent its Return, in which Case it shall not be a Law.
